current_task_corrections.correction: Change the denial_rate component's denominator parameter from 'all_claims' to 'adjudicated_claims'. This excludes pending claims and correctly computes denial rates over only those claims that have reached a final status (Paid, Denied, or Adjusted).
The incorrect denominator choice caused the denial rate value to be understated. Applying the denominator correction above (adjudicated_claims) will produce the correct denial rate value.

Change the monthly_trend component's date_column parameter from 'adjudication_date' to 'service_date_from'. This reflects when care actually occurred rather than when claims were processed, providing a more accurate picture of service volume trends.

reusable_lessons.lesson: When computing denial or adjustment rates in claims analysis, use 'adjudicated_claims' as the denominator, which includes only claims with final statuses (Paid, Denied, Adjusted). Do not include Pended claims in the denominator, as they have not yet reached a terminal status and including them understates the true rate. Always explicitly record the denominator choice in rate metrics.

When constructing monthly trend analyses of claims data, key the time series on 'service_date_from' (when care began) rather than 'adjudication_date' (when the claim was decided). Adjudication dates lag service dates and can create temporal inconsistencies. Service date provides a more stable and business-relevant view of historical trends.
